name: German BMBF Quantum Technologies Programme
description: The German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMFTR, formerly BMBF) is the lead ministry for federal quantum technology funding. The federal government's 2023 action plan commits EUR 3 billion to quantum technologies through 2026, of which EUR 1.37 billion sits with the lead research ministry and around EUR 800 million with state-financed research institutes; an earlier commitment of roughly EUR 2 billion came through the 2020 economic stimulus package. The initiative includes the Quantum Systems research programme, funding for six hardware demonstrator platforms, and the Quantum Future talent pipeline for students and junior researchers.
provider: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)

news.title: BMFTR selects QUDORA-led NFQC-1k consortium for about EUR 122 million trapped-ion project
news.excerpt: The Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space (BMFTR) selected the NFQC-1k trapped-ion quantum computer project, led by QUDORA, under Germany's Quantum Computing Competition. The project has a volume of roughly EUR 122 million, funded for up to five years through the Quantum Systems research programme, with partners including TU Braunschweig, Leibniz University Hannover, PTB, NXP Semiconductors Germany, Forschungszentrum Juelich and AQT Germany.

news.title: Six consortia advance in BMFTR fault-tolerant quantum computing competition worth up to EUR 640 million
news.excerpt: Six industrial and academic consortia, two each for neutral-atom, trapped-ion and superconducting platforms, advanced through the outline phase of BMFTR's mission-driven hardware competition for fault-tolerant quantum computing with pilot-line development. The competition carries up to EUR 640 million in national funding; selected consortia must demonstrate entry systems by 31 March 2027, with a goal of at least two fault-tolerant QPUs by 2030.
